newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW - Sumitomo option risk lingers.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Sumitomo option risk lingers.

text.p: The chairman of the BZW Metals and Energy Group, Christopher Green, said on Monday some of the option risks entered into by Sumitomo Corp of Japan may still be lingering in the copper market.

"There may still be some of the original option risks entered into by Sumitomo Corp but transferred outside to some other entity," Green told Reuters at a metals conference partly organised by the Copper Development Centre in Singapore.

"It is possible that there is still some reverberating influence of these outstanding things. But I would have thought today it would be quite faint and overtaken by other outstanding option strategies," he said. "There are probably still some of those risks out on the marketplace."
BZW Metals and Energy Group is part of BZW, the investment banking division of Britain's Barclays Bank Plc.
Sumitomo was hit just over a year ago by massive losses from unauthorised deals by its former star copper trader, Yasuo Hamanaka. The losses eventually ballooned to an estimated US$2.6 billion.
Green said Sumitomo "no longer, in my opinion, has any outstanding risk positions arising from the Hamanaka affair. They've cleaned up their positions."
Sumitomo has pinned the enormous losses on Hamanaka, who is on trial in Japan after pleading guilty to fraud and forgery.
Investigators are still trying to make sense of an extremely complex web of deals engineered by Hamanaka which spanned the globe. Experts feel the process could take years.
Some of those option positions may extended out to two years forward although Green believes "very few went beyond the middle of 1998."
He said Sumitomo is now engaged in rebuilding their copper business although "in a much better controlled environment than was the base before."
